outcome: No settlement of either open direction for general compact sets is recorded since 26 January 2024. The in-window events are: a partial result on the open direction for two restricted classes (Dąbrowski, arXiv 2408.03919, August 2024); a restricted Vitushkin-related claim that has not been refereed (Tasso, arXiv 2206.14044 v4, August 2025); a 2026 ICM survey that reports the general problem as open (Tolsa, arXiv 2607.16457, July 2026); and a new family of examples in the direction already known to fail (Chang, Dąbrowski, Del Nin, arXiv 2609.33557, September 2026).
problem_asks: The bullet, as Wikipedia words it: 'Vitushkin's conjecture on compact subsets of ℂ with analytic capacity 0'. The Analysis bullet links to the 'Vitushkin's conjecture' section of the Analytic capacity article, which states it for compact K ⊂ ℂ as: γ(K) = 0 if and only if ∫₀^π H¹(proj_θ K) dθ = 0, where proj_θ(x,y) = x cos θ + y sin θ and γ is analytic capacity. The bullet's wording does not say which formulation is meant, so the parts are listed separately. (A) For every compact K ⊂ ℂ: γ(K) = 0 ⇒ ∫H¹(proj_θ K)dθ = 0. Equivalently Fav(K) > 0 ⇒ γ(K) > 0; Dąbrowski (2408.03919, §1.2) calls this Question 1.8. (B) For every compact K ⊂ ℂ: ∫H¹(proj_θ K)dθ = 0 ⇒ γ(K) = 0. Equivalently γ(K) > 0 ⇒ Fav(K) > 0. A and B are not symmetric. (C) The rectifiable-curve form, which the Analytic capacity article and the literature also call Vitushkin's conjecture: for compact E ⊂ ℂ with H¹(E) < ∞, γ(E) = 0 if and only if H¹(E ∩ Γ) = 0 for every rectifiable curve Γ. (D) The same rectifiable-curve criterion for arbitrary compact sets, with no length assumption. Out of scope for this bullet, and recorded only as context: Vitushkin's semi-additivity question for γ (answered by Tolsa, 2002/2003) and whether the semi-additivity constant can be 1.

events.what_happened: A. G. Vitushkin, 'The analytic capacity of sets in problems of approximation theory', Russian Math. Surveys 22:6 (1967), 139–200. This is where the conjecture originates: a compact planar set has positive analytic capacity if and only if its Favard length is positive (Parts A and B together). The 1967 paper itself was not opened. The statement is taken from Dąbrowski (arXiv 2408.03919, §1.2, citing [Vit67]) and from the Wikipedia Analytic capacity article.
events.delivers: None. States the conjecture and proves nothing toward it.
events.remains: All of problem_asks: A, B, C and D.
events.direction: Posits the projection criterion: Parts A and B both hold.

events.what_happened: John B. Garnett, 'Positive length but zero analytic capacity', Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 24 (1970). The Wikipedia Analytic capacity article credits Garnett's 1970 paper with a counterexample: a compact set of positive length and zero analytic capacity. The Garnett paper itself was not opened; its title and venue come from a search result.
events.delivers: Exhibits a compact set of positive length with zero analytic capacity, so zero capacity does not force zero H¹ measure. This rules out the naive converse of the rectifiable-curve idea. It does not bear on Parts A, B, C or D as stated, which concern projections or purely unrectifiable sets.
events.direction: Counterexample to a naive 'zero capacity implies zero length' guess. Not a counterexample to A or B.
events.object: A compact planar set of positive length with zero analytic capacity. Its construction was not read.

events.what_happened: Calderón's 1977 result, cited as [Cal77] in Dąbrowski (arXiv 2408.03919, §1.2). That paper states that Question 1.8 (Part A) is positive for sets of σ-finite length by [Cal77] and [Tol03]. The Calderón paper itself was not opened, and I did not verify its title or venue.
events.delivers: Per Dąbrowski §1.2, establishes Part A (Fav(E) > 0 ⇒ γ(E) > 0) for compact sets of finite length. Together with David (1998), gives the finite-length case of C.
events.remains: Part A for sets of infinite length. Part B for finite length is covered by David (1998) and is not part of this event.
events.direction: Supports Part A for finite-length sets.

events.what_happened: Pertti Mattila, 'Smooth maps, null-sets for integralgeometric measure and analytic capacity', Annals of Mathematics 123(2) (1986), 303–309. Secondary sources (Wikipedia Analytic capacity, and the 2026 Tolsa survey as read through a summarising fetch) say that Mattila showed the projection criterion false for sets without σ-finite length, and that zero Favard length is not preserved under conformal maps while removability is. The paper does not say which implication fails. The Annals paper itself was not opened.
events.delivers: Refutes the projection iff in general, for sets without σ-finite length. It does not determine whether A or B is the failing implication, per secondary sources. Does not settle A or B for any class.
events.remains: Parts A and B for general compact sets: both are left open as far as this paper's statement goes.

checked_by.who: Annals of Mathematics (editors and referees, not named)
checked_by.qualification: Journal of record for the result

events.direction: Refutes the projection iff for non-σ-finite sets, without identifying which implication fails.

events.what_happened: Peter W. Jones and Takafumi Murai, 'Positive analytic capacity but zero Buffon needle probability', Pacific J. Math. 133(1) (1988), 99–114. Exhibits a compact set E with zero Buffon-needle probability, which is equivalent to zero Favard length, and with positive analytic capacity. The Wikipedia article spells the second author 'Muray'. The MSP listing (search result, not opened) gives receipt on 27 March 1987 and publication on 1 May 1988. I found no preprint, so the first public appearance is taken as the 1988 publication.
events.delivers: Refutes Part B in general: there is a compact E with Fav(E) = 0 and γ(E) > 0. By David's theorem (1998), for finite-length sets Fav = 0 forces pure unrectifiability and hence zero capacity, so any such E must have infinite H¹ measure. That inference is mine and was not stated in the sources I read. Does not touch Part A.
events.remains: Part A for general compact sets. Part D for general compact sets. Part B for finite length is already settled, by David.

checked_by.who: Pacific Journal of Mathematics (referees, not named)
checked_by.qualification: Journal of record for the result

events.direction: Refutes Part B (Fav = 0 does not imply γ = 0) for general compact sets.
events.object: A compact set E ⊂ ℂ with zero Favard length (zero Buffon-needle probability) and positive analytic capacity. The abstract states the existence claim. The construction was not read, so I cannot say whether it is explicit or relies on a non-constructive argument.

events.what_happened: Guy David, 'Unrectifiable 1-sets have vanishing analytic capacity', Revista Matemática Iberoamericana 14(2) (1998), 369–479, DOI 10.4171/RMI/242. The EMS abstract states that it completes the proof of Vitushkin's conjecture: for compact E ⊂ ℂ with H¹(E) < ∞, E has vanishing analytic capacity if and only if E is purely unrectifiable. The method is a Menger-curvature rectifiability criterion and a generalisation of the T(b)-theorem to non-homogeneous spaces. Wikipedia dates the result to 1998. One search summary attributed 1997 to the same result in an arXiv text, which I did not verify. I could not verify a preprint or a 1991 Orsay preprint. Orsay preprint 90 (24 Dec 1998) is an expository text, not the proof.
events.delivers: For compact E ⊂ ℂ with H¹(E) < ∞: E purely unrectifiable ⇒ γ(E) = 0. This is Part B for finite length. Together with Calderón (1977), which gives Part A for finite length, it establishes the finite-length criterion (C). Covers finite-length sets only.
events.remains: Parts A and B for sets of infinite length. Part D. Part A for general compact sets.

checked_by.who: Revista Matemática Iberoamericana (referees and editors, not named)

events.direction: Confirms the finite-length criterion (C). For finite length, pure unrectifiability implies zero capacity, which is Part B there.

events.what_happened: Helen Joyce and Peter Mörters, 'A set with finite curvature and projections of zero length', preprint 1999 (TU Kaiserslautern repository, server date 3 April 2000). Published as J. Math. Anal. Appl. 247(1) (2000), 126–135, DOI 10.1006/jmaa.2000.6831 (journal details from a search result, not opened). The repository page I opened gives only the opening sentences of the abstract. Per secondary sources, the paper constructs a compact non-removable set that is purely unrectifiable (meets every rectifiable curve in zero length), with Hausdorff dimension 1. It also has zero projections, per the title. Wikipedia calls this example easier than Jones–Murai and says it uses curvature of measures.
events.revisions: Preprint 1999 (Kaiserslautern repository, server date 2000-04-03); journal version JMAA 247(1), 2000.
events.delivers: Refutes Part D: a purely unrectifiable compact set of positive analytic capacity, so the rectifiable-curve criterion fails without a length assumption (per secondary sources). Also gives a second example for Part B, from the title. Neither is verified against the body.
events.remains: Part A for general compact sets. Part B is already known to fail. Part C (finite length) is unaffected and is settled by David.

checked_by.who: Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications (referees, not named)
checked_by.qualification: Refereed journal of record; journal details from a search result

events.direction: Refutes Part D (purely unrectifiable does not imply zero capacity without finite length). Also refutes Part B again.
events.object: A compact set E ⊂ ℂ of Hausdorff dimension 1 that is purely unrectifiable with positive analytic capacity, built from measures of finite curvature (per secondary sources and the title). The construction was not read.

events.what_happened: F. Nazarov, S. Treil and A. Volberg, 'The Tb-theorem on non-homogeneous spaces that proves a conjecture of Vitushkin'. Written in 1999 and issued as CRM (Barcelona) preprint 519 in 2000, according to the arXiv abstract. Posted to arXiv as 1401.2479 on 10 January 2014 (v2 17 January 2014). The arXiv abstract states: 'Formally this paper is a proof of the (qualitative version of the) Vitushkin conjecture.' Its final section gives a quantitative version, which Tolsa used for semi-additivity. The abstract also says the CRM preprint was removed from the CRM archive.
events.delivers: A second, Tb-theorem-based proof of the finite-length criterion (C): for compact E ⊂ ℂ with H¹(E) < ∞, E is purely unrectifiable if and only if γ(E) = 0, per the abstract's 'qualitative version'. I have not verified that it covers both directions for finite length. Restricted to finite length.
events.remains: Parts A, B and D for sets of infinite length.
events.direction: Confirms the finite-length criterion (C), by a different route from David's.

events.what_happened: Xavier Tolsa, 'Painlevé's problem and the semiadditivity of analytic capacity', arXiv math/0204027 (2 April 2002); Acta Mathematica 190 (2003), 105–149. The arXiv abstract says that γ is comparable with γ₊ (the capacity defined through Cauchy transforms of positive measures), with absolute constants. It characterises removable sets via curvature of measures, which solves Painlevé's problem, and deduces that γ is semi-additive, 'which solves a long standing question of Vitushkin'.
events.delivers: Does not address Parts A or B for general sets. Proves Vitushkin's semi-additivity question, which is outside this bullet. Per Dąbrowski (2408.03919 §1.2) and the Wikipedia Analytic capacity article, Tolsa's work together with David's gives the conjecture for σ-finite length, and Part A for σ-finite length.
events.remains: Part A for non-σ-finite sets. Part B for non-σ-finite sets is already known to fail. The constant-1 subadditivity question is outside this bullet.

checked_by.who: Acta Mathematica (referees and editors, not named)
checked_by.qualification: Journal of record for the result

events.direction: Supports Part A and Part B for σ-finite sets, through the σ-finite theory. Does not address non-σ-finite sets.

events.what_happened: Alan Chang and Xavier Tolsa, 'Analytic capacity and projections', arXiv 1712.00594 (v1 2 December 2017; v2 20 January 2019); Journal of the European Mathematical Society 22(12) (2020), 4121–4159. The arXiv abstract page (summarised, not verbatim) proves that for compact E ⊂ ℂ and a Borel measure μ supported on E, γ(E) is bounded below by a constant times μ(E)² divided by the integral over an arbitrary interval I of angles of the squared L² norms of the projections of μ. It also has a higher-dimensional extension with signed Riesz kernels. The paper says it is related to Vitushkin's conjecture.
events.delivers: Partial progress on Part A: a positive-capacity conclusion whenever E carries a measure whose projections are L²-large on an interval of directions. That is a measure-level hypothesis, stronger than Fav(E) > 0, so it does not settle Part A for general compact sets (Dąbrowski §1.2 says the same).
events.remains: Part A for general compact sets. Part B untouched.

checked_by.who: Journal of the European Mathematical Society (referees and editors, not named)

events.direction: Partial support for Part A, under a measure-level hypothesis.

events.what_happened: Alan Chang, Damian Dąbrowski, Tuomas Orponen and Michele Villa, 'Structure of sets with nearly maximal Favard length', arXiv 2203.01279 (v1 2 March 2022); Analysis & PDE 17 (2024), 1473–1500. The abstract: if E ⊂ B(1) ⊂ ℝ² is H¹-measurable with H¹(E) < ∞ and Fav(E) ≥ Fav(L) − δ for a segment L of the same length, then E is covered by an ε-Lipschitz graph up to length ε, with ε = Cδ^{1/70}. The abstract does not mention analytic capacity or Vitushkin's conjecture.
events.delivers: Nothing about γ. It is a structural result on sets with near-maximal Favard length, so it is discounted for this bullet. Recorded because it sits in the Favard-length literature the open direction depends on.

checked_by.who: Analysis & PDE (referees and editors, not named)

events.direction: No bearing on γ, so no direction for this bullet.

events.what_happened: Damian Dąbrowski and Michele Villa, 'Analytic capacity and dimension of sets with plenty of big projections', arXiv 2204.05804 (v1 12 April 2022; v2 21 June 2024, a reorganisation that leaves the main results unchanged and supersedes arXiv 2109.10087); Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 378(6) (2025), 3897–3950, DOI 10.1090/tran/9265. The abstract: 'Our main result marks progress on an old conjecture of Vitushkin.' A compact planar set with plenty of big projections (PBP) has positive analytic capacity, with a quantitative lower bound. There is a higher-dimensional Riesz-kernel version, including Lipschitz harmonic capacity, and an Analyst's Traveling Salesman Theorem for PBP sets.
events.revisions: v1 2022-04-12; v2 2024-06-21 (reorganisation, main results unchanged); TAMS 378(6), 2025.
events.delivers: Part A for compact planar sets with plenty of big projections: positive analytic capacity, with a quantitative lower bound. Restricted to the PBP class, which is a strong hypothesis. Does not address Part A for general compact sets, nor Part B.
events.remains: Part A for general compact sets. Part B. Part D.

checked_by.who: Transactions of the American Mathematical Society (referees and editors, not named)

events.direction: Partial support for Part A, under the PBP hypothesis.

events.what_happened: Damian Dąbrowski, 'Favard length and quantitative rectifiability', arXiv 2408.03919 (v1 7 August 2024; the only version listed). Abstract: for Ahlfors 1-regular E with large Favard length, E contains a big piece of a Lipschitz graph, which is a quantitative Besicovitch projection theorem; this answers questions of David–Semmes and Peres–Solomyak; 'We also make progress on Vitushkin's conjecture.' Body (read from the HTML): Corollary 1.11 says that a compact set satisfying uniformly large Favard length (ULFL) has γ(E) ≳_κ diam(E), without assuming H¹(E) < ∞. Corollary 1.12 says that a compact Ahlfors-regular set with Fav(E) ≥ κ diam(E) has γ(E) ≳_{κ,A} diam(E), using Theorem 1.1 and Verdera's quantitative Denjoy theorem. Remark 1.10 says the best dependence would be linear, γ(E) ≳ Fav(E). §1.2 states Question 1.8: 'Suppose that E ⊂ ℝ² is compact. Is it true that Fav(E) > 0 ⇒ γ(E) > 0?' It is positive for σ-finite length (Calderón 1977; Tolsa 2003) and otherwise open. The paper says it does not give a general answer.
events.revisions: v1 only, per the arXiv listing. No journal publication found.
events.delivers: Part A for two restricted classes: (i) compact sets with uniformly large Favard length at all scales, with no finite-length assumption, giving γ ≳ diam; (ii) compact Ahlfors-regular sets with Fav ≥ κ·diam, giving γ ≳ diam. Constants depend on κ and, in (ii), on the Ahlfors constant. Does not cover general compact sets with merely positive Favard length, and does not address Part B.
events.remains: Part A for general compact sets (Question 1.8 is still open, per the paper itself). Part B, which is false. Part D. The linear dependence γ ≳ Fav (Remark 1.10).
events.time_since_posted: about 26 months as of 13 October 2026, with no journal publication, referee report or independent verification found
events.direction: Toward Part A (positive Favard length forces positive capacity), restricted to the classes in delivers. Does not contradict anything in problem_asks.

events.what_happened: Emanuele Tasso, 'Rectifiability of a class of integral geometric measures and applications', arXiv 2206.14044. The main theorem, on the rectifiability of Federer's integral-geometric measure for exponent p > 1, is unchanged since v1 (28 June 2022). The Vitushkin applications first appear in v4 (11 August 2025). The v1, v2 and v3 abstracts do not mention Vitushkin; the v3 abstract (1 February 2023) lists two main consequences, Federer's problem and a slicing criterion. The v4 abstract says 'the exposition and applications have been substantially revised to highlight the result's consequences for Vitushkin's conjecture on analytic capacity and removability in the complex plane', and that the slicing criterion has been removed and 'will appear in separate work'. The v4 abstract claims two results: (a) 'in a multi-scale setting, we provide an affirmative answer for sets with finite integral geometric measure within regimes of Favard length behavior at small scales not previously addressed'; (b) in a single-scale setting, an extension of the Besicovitch–Federer projection theorem to planar sets meeting a typical line in finitely many points. Per a summarising fetch of the v4 HTML (about half the text read): Theorem 1.2 takes ℐ¹₁(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊂ ℂ, with an Orlicz-type Favard lower bound at small scales around each point, and gives positive analytic capacity. Corollary 1.4 handles the single-scale case. Talks on this topic (GMTCortona, 21 June 2024; Barcelona Analysis Seminar, 31 October 2024, listing says 'a part of Vitushkin's conjecture still not completely understood') are not written arguments and do not set the date.
events.revisions: v1 2022-06-28 (main theorem); v2 2022-09-20; v3 2023-02-01 (no Vitushkin content in abstract); v4 2025-08-11 (Vitushkin applications added; slicing criterion removed).
events.delivers: Part A (Fav > 0 ⇒ γ > 0, equivalently γ = 0 ⇒ Fav = 0) for two restricted classes, per the v4 abstract: (a) compact K ⊂ ℂ with ℐ¹₁(K) < ∞, at small scales, under a Favard-length lower bound; (b) planar sets meeting a typical line in finitely many points. The abstract does not state which formulation of Vitushkin's conjecture is meant. The v4 HTML summary says it uses the projection form. Not verified against the body. Does not address Part B, general compact sets, or Part D.
events.remains: Part A outside the ℐ¹₁-finite and typical-line classes. Part B (already false in general). Part D. The general iff.
events.time_since_posted: about 14 months (v4) as of 13 October 2026. No journal publication, review or zbMATH entry found.
events.doubts: Two points for the judging pass, not verdicts. (1) The Vitushkin applications first appear in v4. The v4 abstract says a slicing criterion present in earlier versions has been removed, so the scope has changed between versions. (2) Whether a finite ℐ¹₁ measure already implies that H¹ is σ-finite. If it does, the class in (a) is already covered by Calderón (1977) and Tolsa (2003), and the new content is less than it appears. I did not establish this either way.
events.direction: Toward Part A, for the two restricted classes in delivers. The abstract claims an 'affirmative answer' in those regimes.

events.what_happened: Caleb Marshall, 'Improved power laws for the Favard length problem in all dimensions', arXiv 2509.02882 (v1 2 September 2025). Quantitative upper bounds on the Favard length of neighbourhoods of purely 1-unrectifiable rational product Cantor sets in ℝ^d, d ≥ 2. Applied to the four-corner Cantor set, the bound is N^{-1/5+u} for every u > 0. The abstract does not mention analytic capacity, Vitushkin's conjecture or removable sets.
events.revisions: v1 2025-09-02; a later version (Aug 2026) per a search result, not opened.
events.delivers: Nothing about γ. Favard-length decay for specific Cantor sets. Discounted for this bullet.
events.direction: No bearing on γ, so no direction for this bullet.

events.what_happened: Marina Fernàndez-Vilaseca, 'A Tb type theorem for suppressed kernels', arXiv 2606.26401 (v1 24 June 2026). A non-homogeneous Tb-type theorem for Calderón–Zygmund singular integral operators in arbitrary dimension, extending the planar Cauchy-transform theorem of Nazarov, Treil and Volberg. The abstract does not mention Vitushkin's conjecture, analytic capacity or Favard length.
events.revisions: v1 2026-06-24 only, per the abstract page.
events.delivers: Nothing about this bullet. A higher-dimensional harmonic-analysis tool. Discounted.
events.direction: No bearing on γ for this bullet.

events.what_happened: Xavier Tolsa, 'Interactions between quantitative rectifiability, singular integrals, and boundary value problems for harmonic functions', arXiv 2607.16457 (v1 17 July 2026; v2 21 July 2026). Proceedings of the ICM 2026, Vol. 2 (Plenary Lectures), pp. 313–340, DOI 10.1137/25M1804054. A survey with no new claimed result on this bullet. Per a summarising fetch of the first ~100,000 characters of the HTML (the PDF was unreadable), the survey says that Vitushkin's conjecture is settled for finite-length sets by David (1998), that Dąbrowski (2024) solved the quantitative Besicovitch projection problem, and that the open direction of Vitushkin's conjecture remains open, with unclear prospects for Dąbrowski's techniques. These quotes are unverified. The abstract page does not mention the topic.
events.delivers: No new result on this bullet. Expert status statement only: the finite-length case is settled and the open direction is open, per the summarised text.
events.remains: Every part the survey reports as open: the open direction of Part A for general compact sets.
events.direction: Reports Part A as open in general, and the finite-length case as settled.

events.what_happened: Alan Chang, Damian Dąbrowski and Giacomo Del Nin, 'Favard length of non-homogeneous random disc-like Cantor sets', arXiv 2609.33557 (v1 27 September 2026; the only version listed). The abstract: sharp estimates for the Favard-length decay of a random variant of Garnett's non-homogeneous four-corner Cantor sets; sharpness of Mattila's lower bound on Favard length in terms of Riesz capacity; and 'a new family of examples of sets with positive analytic capacity and zero Favard length'. Body (from the HTML, partially read): Theorem 1.14 gives γ(K_n) ≈ (Σ_{k≤n} θ_k²)^{-1/2} for the finite-stage sets, θ_k = 4^{-k}/r_k, for any admissible radii and any choice of rotations. Corollary 1.15: if Σθ_k = ∞ and Σθ_k² < ∞ (for example r_k = k·4^{-k}), then γ(K) > 0 and almost surely Fav(K) = 0. §1.5 states that Fav(E) > 0 ⇒ γ(E) > 0 'remains an open problem', known only for σ-finite length. The paper does not resolve it.
events.revisions: v1 only, per the arXiv listing.
events.delivers: Part B fails again, with a new family: random Cantor sets in ℂ with γ > 0 and Fav = 0 almost surely, under Σθ_k = ∞ and Σθ_k² < ∞. By the same inference as for Jones–Murai, such sets must have infinite H¹ measure, since finite-length sets obey David's theorem. The paper does not say this. No bearing on Part A, which the paper calls open.
events.remains: Part A for general compact sets (open per the paper). Part D. Part B is already known to fail, so this adds only further counterexamples.
events.direction: Cuts against Part B, which was already known to fail. No bearing on Part A.
events.object: A random four-corner-type Cantor set K ⊂ ℂ built from a sequence of radii r_k and independent random rotations. If Σθ_k = ∞ and Σθ_k² < ∞ (θ_k = 4^{-k}/r_k), then γ(K) > 0 and almost surely Fav(K) = 0. The existence statement is probabilistic (an almost-sure statement over random rotations), so the set is non-constructive and is not explicit. Theorem 1.14 gives the capacity of the finite-stage sets K_n for every choice of rotations.

disputes.summary: 'Vitushkin's conjecture' is used for two formulations. The first is the projection (Favard-length) criterion, which the Analytic capacity article gives as the statement (Parts A and B). The second is the rectifiable-curve criterion, which David (1998) proves for finite length (Part C) and which the same article also calls Vitushkin's conjecture. The Wikipedia bullet's wording does not say which is meant. This record covers all four parts.

Mattila (1986): secondary sources say the projection criterion is false for sets without σ-finite length, but they differ on what Mattila established. One says he showed that the Favard property is not conformally invariant, another says he disproved the integral-geometric null-set version. The sources also differ on which implication fails. Jones–Murai (1988) identifies the failing implication as Part B. The primary Mattila text was not read.

David's theorem: Wikipedia dates the result to 1998 (RMI 14). One search summary attributed 1997 to the same result in an arXiv text. I did not verify the 1997 attribution and did not resolve the discrepancy. The record uses 1998.

Tasso (v4, August 2025) claims 'an affirmative answer' for sets with finite integral-geometric measure at small scales. The abstract does not say which formulation or which direction is meant. A 2024 talk listing describes its subject as 'a part of Vitushkin's conjecture still not completely understood'. The scope of the claim is therefore not settled by the sources I read.

summary: I ran 42 web searches and opened the arXiv abstract or HTML page for each main work, plus the Wikipedia list and Analytic capacity articles, the EMS page for David (1998), the Kaiserslautern repository record for Joyce–Mörters, and the CORDIS page for the EU project QuRe-ViMaL. Primary texts for Vitushkin (1967), Garnett (1970), Calderón (1977), Mattila (1986) and Jones–Murai (1988) were not opened, so their content comes from secondary sources and is flagged per event. The statement's bullet links to the projection criterion in the Analytic capacity article, which is what I have recorded as Parts A and B. Part B (Fav = 0 ⇒ γ = 0) is false in general (Jones–Murai 1988; Joyce–Mörters 1999/2000; a further family in Chang–Dąbrowski–Del Nin, September 2026). Part A (γ = 0 ⇒ Fav = 0, or Fav > 0 ⇒ γ > 0, Dąbrowski's Question 1.8) is open for general compact sets. It is known for σ-finite length (Calderón 1977; Tolsa 2003). The finite-length rectifiable-curve criterion (C) is settled (David 1998; a second proof by Nazarov–Treil–Volberg, CRM 2000 / arXiv 2014). Partial progress on Part A before the window: Chang–Tolsa (2017/2020) and Dąbrowski–Villa (2022/2025). In the window, three events are recorded. Dąbrowski (7 August 2024) proves Part A for uniformly-large-Favard sets and for Ahlfors-regular sets with Fav ≥ κ·diam, and says explicitly that Question 1.8 is still open; nothing is found to show that this has been refereed or published after 26 months. Tasso (v4, 11 August 2025) adds Vitushkin-related Part A claims for ℐ¹₁-finite sets at small scales and for sets meeting a typical line in finitely many points. These are not refereed, and the Vitushkin content first appears in v4, when a slicing criterion was removed. I could not establish whether ℐ¹₁-finite implies H¹-σ-finite, which would make the first class already covered. Tolsa's ICM survey (July 2026) reports the general problem as open, but that is from a summarising fetch of the HTML, since the PDF was unreadable. Chang–Dąbrowski–Del Nin (September 2026) give a new family of Part B counterexamples and state that Question 1.8 is open. Their acknowledgements credit the MSCA project QuReViMal (grant 101108515), which is the CORDIS record for the project whose first objective is this conjecture. That is a funding link, not a result, and the project ended on 31 January 2026. I found no outcome report. On AI: no event names an AI system or credits one with mathematics. The only AI sentence in the in-window papers I read is 'LLMs were used to generate some of the figures and for proofreading' in Chang–Dąbrowski–Del Nin, which names no system and is peripheral, so their ai.none_found is false with empty systems. The AI searches (Vitushkin with AI terms; AlphaEvolve; GPT-5; Gemini Deep Think, AlphaProof and Aristotle; Erdős-problem trackers; the OpenAI proof audit; Sra's counterexample paper 2608.29595, abstract only) found nothing on this problem. Close calls: whether Tasso's ℐ¹₁ class is already σ-finite; whether Dąbrowski's ULFL corollary counts as movement on Question 1.8 or only as a restricted case; and whether the Tolsa survey's status sentence is accurate, which I could not verify verbatim.
competing_reading: Read 'Vitushkin's conjecture' as the rectifiable-curve criterion (C/D). On that reading the bullet was settled for finite length by David in 1998, is false for general sets by Joyce–Mörters (1999/2000), and nothing in the window changes its status. Alternatively, read the bullet as the projection iff (A and B). Then the in-window items (Dąbrowski 2024, Tasso v4) are partial movement on the open direction A, not no change, and Dąbrowski's Corollaries 1.11 and 1.12 are a real if restricted advance. A third reading: Tasso's ℐ¹₁-finite class may already be inside σ-finite length, in which case its Part A claim is not new for that class. The judging pass would then rest on whether the ℐ¹₁ result is genuinely beyond σ-finite sets.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The full text of Tasso arXiv 2206.14044 v4: the exact statement of Theorem 1.2 and Corollary 1.4, which formulation and direction are proved, and whether ℐ¹₁(K) < ∞ implies H¹-σ-finiteness. (2) The rest of Dąbrowski arXiv 2408.03919, including the acknowledgements, to check for any AI sentence, and any journal acceptance. (3) The PDF of Tolsa arXiv 2607.16457 for the exact wording of the status sentence on the open direction. (4) Referee reports or journal decisions for Tasso v4 and Dąbrowski 2408. (5) The primary text of Mattila (1986) and of Joyce–Mörters, to confirm which implication each refutes and how.
